# The Seven Sisters and the God Who Gathers

## Scripture
*"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name. Great is our Lord and mighty in power; his understanding has no limit."* — Psalm 147:4-5

## Reflection
Step outside on an October evening and look up toward the east. You'll find the Pleiades—the Seven Sisters—a tight cluster of stars that has captured human attention for millennia. On a clear night, most people can spot six or seven of its brightest stars, though the cluster actually contains over a thousand. What appears as a small, sparkling knot is really a vast family bound together by gravity, traveling through space as one.

There's something tender in how Scripture describes God's relationship to the stars: He calls them each by name. Not just the bright ones. Not just the ones we can see. Every single one, in every distant cluster, known and named by the One who made them.

If God's understanding has no limit—if He numbers and names the countless stars—then surely He knows the details of your life that feel too small or too tangled to matter. The Pleiades remind us that what looks like a smudge of light to us is a carefully ordered family to Him. You are not lost in the vastness. You are known, gathered, and called by name.

## Prayer
Lord of the stars, You who name each one and hold them in their places, thank You for knowing us with that same intimate care. When we feel small or overlooked, remind us that Your understanding has no limit and Your attention never wanders. Gather us close, as You gather the Seven Sisters, and let us shine for Your glory. Amen.
